meta.scope: Browser-driving AI agent/framework comparison matrix (NOT cloud browser $/hour infra pricing)
meta.timezone_note: Row dates are the pass that last read that row. Latest pass 2026-11-02 added five rows. Older rows keep their own last_checked. Demo URLs on the new rows were checked 2026-11-02.
meta.disclaimer: All fields gathered from public docs/repos only. Prefer unknown over guessing. Prices and capabilities may change; re-check sources before publishing.

coverage.en: This matrix is a curated seed plus a weekly scan. It is not exhaustive. Misses are welcome.
coverage.zh: 这张表是精选种子，加上每周扫描，并不穷尽。漏记的欢迎指出。

entries.name: Browser Use
entries.perception_note: Public codebase/docs describe a DOM/accessibility serialization pipeline plus screenshots for the agent (DOMWatchdog / DOM serializer + screenshot path).
entries.hosting_note: Open-source library runs locally with Chrome/CDP; Browser Use Cloud offers hosted agents API and stealth browsers.
entries.mcp_note: Hosted MCP at https://api.browser-use.com/v3/mcp (task-level tools); local stdio browser-harness-mcp for step-by-step control of logged-in Chrome.
entries.auth_model_detail: Local harness can drive the user's Chrome session; Cloud uses managed browsers/profiles and API keys. Exact secret-vault behavior varies by path — see OSS sensitive-data docs.
entries.anti_bot: Cloud stealth browsers claim 90.5% pass rate on Stealth Bench V2 (100 bot-protected sites); CAPTCHA solving advertised for Cloud (reCAPTCHA; hCaptcha newer/not guaranteed); off in EU region per marketing page.
entries.pricing_summary: OSS free (MIT). Cloud: pay-as-you-go — $0.02/hour browsers + $5/GB residential proxy; agents billed model tokens +20% service fee + browser time/traffic; $1 free credit for eligible new signups. Source: browser-use.com/pricing (accessed 2026-10-19).

entries.name: Stagehand
entries.perception_note: Docs/marketing emphasize hybrid accessibility-tree trimming; observe/act/extract use a11y+DOM context; optional CUA/agent modes can use vision models when configured.
entries.hosting_note: localBrowser.launch / CDP attach for local; browserbase.launch for Browserbase cloud (stealth, proxies, Model Gateway, server-side cache).
entries.mcp_note: CLI-agent MCP adapter exists in-repo (stdio: run/snapshot/screenshot) but docs call integrations experimental and not published as a standalone package. Browserbase also documents hosted MCP with Stagehand-style tools (navigate/act/observe/extract) — treat as Browserbase-hosted path.
entries.auth_model_detail: Caller supplies model API keys (or Browserbase Model Gateway). Browser session auth is whatever cookies/storage the local or Browserbase context holds; no first-party 'credential vault' product called out in Stagehand quickstart.
entries.anti_bot: When run on Browserbase, inherits Browserbase stealth/proxy/session features (see Browserbase docs). Stagehand itself is an SDK, not a stealth browser vendor.
entries.pricing_summary: No Stagehand $/hour. The SDK is MIT; local runs pay your model provider. Cloud runs bill on Browserbase, not on a Stagehand price. Browserbase pricing read 2026-10-24: Free $0, Developer $20/mo, Startup $99/mo, Scale custom. Browser-hour overage on that page: Developer $0.12/hr, Startup $0.10/hr. Those figures are the host, not Stagehand.

entries.name: Skyvern
entries.perception_note: GitHub/README: relies on Vision LLMs / computer vision to interact with sites rather than only brittle DOM/XPath scripts; Playwright-compatible SDK adds AI page commands (act/extract/validate).
entries.hosting_note: Self-host with own LLM keys (pip/Docker/K8s); Skyvern Cloud app + API + hosted MCP.
entries.mcp_note: Hosted MCP https://api.skyvern.com/mcp/ (OAuth or x-api-key); local stdio via skyvern run mcp; large tool surface with optional scopes.
entries.auth_model_detail: Encrypted credential vault; model sees placeholders, real values injected at fill time. Integrates Bitwarden, 1Password, Azure Key Vault, custom HTTP vault. Self-host: credentials stay on your infra except what goes to the LLM provider you configure.
entries.anti_bot: Cloud plans advertise CAPTCHA solvers (basic on Hobby, advanced on Pro), residential proxy / geo options on paid tiers; self-host docs note Cloud proxy/CAPTCHA are not included when self-hosting.
entries.pricing_summary: OSS self-host free aside from your LLM/infra (AGPL-3.0). Cloud credit plans from public pricing: Free 5,000 one-time credits; Hobby $29/mo 30,000 credits; Pro $149/mo 150,000 credits; Enterprise custom. Source: skyvern.com/pricing and docs Billing page (accessed 2026-10-19). Note: pricing FAQ wording on 'run' vs 'credit' has varied across pages — quote the Billing table as primary.

entries.name: Playwright MCP
entries.perception_note: MCP server uses Playwright accessibility snapshots (structured a11y tree), not pixel/vision models, by design.
entries.hosting_note: npm package @playwright/mcp runs locally (npx); drives local browsers. No first-party hosted agent cloud as part of this package.
entries.mcp_note: This product is an MCP server. Docs also mention WebMCP page-registered tools and a separate Playwright CLI+SKILLS path for coding agents.
entries.auth_model_detail: Uses the browser Playwright launches/attaches on the machine running the MCP server; logins are whatever is in that browser profile/context.
entries.anti_bot: No dedicated stealth/CAPTCHA product claimed in Playwright MCP README; inherits ordinary Playwright browser fingerprint behavior unless you add your own tooling.
entries.pricing_summary: Free open source (Apache-2.0). You pay for the LLM/MCP client separately. No Playwright MCP cloud price page.

entries.name: Claude in Chrome
entries.perception_note: Help Center: extension reads page text, can take screenshots, uses debugger permission to click/type/screenshot, and can read console/network/DOM state for debugging. Exact internal a11y-vs-vision mix for every action is not fully specified in consumer docs — marked hybrid.
entries.hosting_note: Chrome extension product tied to Claude paid plans; drives the user's Chrome. Claude Code / Cowork can remote-drive the same extension. Cowork also rolling a built-in desktop browser option.
entries.mcp_note: Not positioned as an MCP server. Integrates via Chrome extension + Claude Code/Cowork connectors. (Anthropic has other MCP connectors elsewhere; this browser product is extension-based.)
entries.auth_model_detail: Shares the user's Chrome login state. Optional 1Password for Claude (beta, macOS): user approves biometrics; Claude never sees password/OTP per Help Center. CAPTCHA/login pages: Claude Code Chrome docs say it pauses for the user to handle.
entries.anti_bot: No public stealth benchmark claimed. Safety classifiers gate actions; prohibited actions include purchases, creating accounts, handling sensitive card/ID data, etc. Site allow/block lists for Team/Enterprise.
entries.pricing_summary: Requires Claude paid plan (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise). No separate per-browser-hour price published on the Claude in Chrome help pages; usage is under Claude subscription (plan prices not restated here — see claude.com/pricing).

entries.name: Notte
entries.perception_note: Read 2026-10-24. session.observe() returns an action space (interaction actions) and a base64 screenshot. Fast perception, the default, lists those actions with IDs and selectors. Agent start takes use_vision, default true: whether to use vision. docs.notte.cc/concepts/bua and docs.notte.cc/features/agents/configuration both served the Anything API page on this date, so the older BUA DOM-plus-screenshot writeup was not re-read there.
entries.hosting_note: Cloud sessions/agents/functions; docs/marketing also mention on-prem for Enterprise. Open-source SDK components on GitHub under SSPL.
entries.mcp_note: MCP server documented (docs.notte.cc/integrations/mcp); Notte Browser MCP via pip install notte-mcp; Agent Skill and CLI also published.
entries.auth_model_detail: Secret Vaults: encrypted credentials; placeholder substitution outside model context on supported fill actions. Personas for digital identities (email/phone/credentials).
entries.anti_bot: Cloud browser sessions marketed with anti-detection, residential proxies, and CAPTCHA solving.
entries.pricing_summary: Plans grant credits + usage rates from notte.cc/pricing (accessed 2026-10-19, not re-fetched on the 2026-10-24 perception pass): Browser Sessions $0.01/hour; Browser Functions $0.05/hour; Residential proxies $10/GB (BYO proxy $0.20/GB on Startup); Free $10 one-time credits; Developer $20/mo; Startup $100/mo; Enterprise custom. LLM tokens: 'No Notte markup when using Notte-managed keys' per pricing page.

entries.name: OpenAI Computer Use / Browser tools
entries.perception_note: ComputerToolset path is screenshot + mouse/keyboard (vision). BrowserToolset path exposes page text/controls as function tools (DOM-like structured reading). App chooses the path.
entries.hosting_note: You supply the browser/desktop driver (local Playwright sample, Browserbase/Stagehand, Browser Use, Daytona, E2B, etc.). Separate Agents API path for OpenAI-hosted browser environment documented elsewhere.
entries.mcp_note: Docs say you may use remote MCP tools as your own UI tools; Computer Use itself is Responses API tools, not a dedicated Playwright-style MCP product.
entries.auth_model_detail: App-owned and driver-dependent, not an OpenAI credential vault. The Responses guide (read 2026-10-24) says your application supplies the driver and owns the session, permissions, and cleanup, and to keep credentials out of page text and screenshots. Partner drivers (Browserbase, Browser Use, Daytona, E2B) keep their own auth. On the separate Agents API hosted browser, your application starts the session and handles sign-in.
entries.anti_bot: Not a stealth product; depends entirely on the environment/driver you attach.
entries.pricing_summary: API token usage (model + image input for screenshots) per OpenAI pricing; environment partners may charge separately. No single computer-use plan price on the guide. The sample-app LICENSE file, read 2026-10-24, is the MIT License, Copyright (c) 2025 OpenAI. The API itself stays a proprietary Responses API.

entries.name: Smooth
entries.perception_note: Read 2026-10-24. Docs describe a hosted natural-language browser agent. The SDK readme says it drives the browser with mouse and keyboard and is not a DOM-manipulation API for the caller. Screenshot is an optional agent tool, and evaluate_js can read the DOM. None of those pages label the agent's own perception as DOM, vision, or a mix.
entries.hosting_note: Hosted serverless API (docs introduction). The same page lists on-prem as an enterprise option. The docs index has no self-host guide.
entries.mcp_note: docs.smooth.sh/llms.txt (2026-10-24) lists REST and CLI and no MCP page. smooth-sdk pyproject.toml has an optional mcp extra (fastmcp) and mcp_config.json imports smooth.mcp.SmoothMCP, which is not in the published source tree.
entries.auth_model_detail: Browser profiles keep cookies and login state. The CLI authentication page says credentials stay on your machine and in profile storage, and the agent does not see the password. This is not a credential vault that injects placeholders.
entries.anti_bot: Docs introduction lists auto-CAPTCHA solvers. Session creation has stealth_mode, default false, described as helping avoid detection, plus optional proxy settings.
entries.pricing_summary: Credit pricing from docs.smooth.sh/pricing (read 2026-10-24). Agent step $0.005 on Free, Starter, and Growth. Free $0 with $5 credits and 2 concurrent browsers. Starter $50/mo with $50 credits and 5 concurrent browsers. Growth $500/mo with $500 credits and 50 concurrent browsers. Enterprise custom. Run Task docs: 1 credit = $0.01. The pricing table's checkmark rows (custom proxy, profiles, BYOC) did not survive as which-tier marks in the markdown fetch, so those cells are not assigned here.

entries.name: ego (lite)
entries.perception_note: README/docs emphasize high-quality page Snapshot (page → structured text) via browser-engine customization; agent acts on snapshot. Not marketed as pixel-vision CUA.
entries.hosting_note: Local desktop browser app (macOS + Windows; Linux roadmap). Data stays on device. Not a cloud browser host.
entries.mcp_note: Primary integration is Agent Skill `ego-browser` (npx skills add citrolabs/ego-lite / auto-written into agent skills dirs). Not positioned as an MCP server in README.
entries.auth_model_detail: Optional Chrome data migration on first launch: sessions, cookies, passwords, extensions, bookmarks stay local for agent Spaces to reuse.
entries.anti_bot: Fewer CAPTCHAs claimed when reusing real login state (comparison table). No public stealth-bench score found this pass.
entries.pricing_summary: Free download; MIT repo. README: zero cost, zero config. No cloud $/hour page found.

entries.name: xbrowser
entries.perception_note: ARIA snapshot + ref system for element targeting; screenshots/snapshots advertised. CLI-first, not a vision-CUA agent framework.
entries.hosting_note: Local CLI driving Chromium via CDP (npm i -g @xbrowser/cli). Not a managed cloud browser product.
entries.mcp_note: Ships Agent Skill URL (https://xbrowser.dev/skills/xbrowser-agent.md) for coding agents. No first-party MCP server page found this pass.
entries.auth_model_detail: CDP connect to running Chrome/Chromium; sessions/daemon; inherits whatever profile the connected browser holds. No cloud credential vault product documented.
entries.anti_bot: Marketing claims CDP firewall / stealth fingerprint hiding and anti-detection. Stealth docs exist in repo (docs/stealth.md). No independent pass-rate published here.
entries.pricing_summary: MIT OSS CLI; npm @xbrowser/cli. No paid cloud plan found on homepage this pass.

entries.name: agent-browser
entries.perception_note: snapshot returns accessibility tree with refs (@e1…); screenshots optional. Explicitly agent-first compact text, not vision-CUA.
entries.hosting_note: Native Rust CLI + daemon controlling local Chrome via CDP (npm/brew/cargo). Docs mention provider-owned cloud browsers as optional attach path — primary product is local CLI.
entries.mcp_note: README documents `agent-browser mcp` stdio MCP server plus experimental WebMCP page tools.
entries.auth_model_detail: Sessions/profiles/cookies/storage; can set HTTP basic credentials. Auth state is local/session — not a cloud vault that redacts secrets from the model.
entries.anti_bot: No dedicated stealth/CAPTCHA product claim found on homepage/README this pass. Ordinary Chrome-for-Testing automation fingerprint unless user adds tooling.
entries.pricing_summary: Apache-2.0 open source; free CLI. No Vercel-billed agent-browser cloud plan on product page.

entries.name: huashu-chrome
entries.perception_note: Chrome extension drives real DOM clicks/fills; returns effect snapshots (what the page became), not a vision-CUA loop. 22 browser tools over MCP.
entries.hosting_note: Local-only: npm CLI + MCP server + 127.0.0.1 bridge + Chrome extension. Docs stress traffic never leaves localhost.
entries.mcp_note: Core product is an MCP server (`npx huashu-chrome mcp`) with install writers for 20+ MCP hosts (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, etc.).
entries.auth_model_detail: Controls the user's everyday Chrome with full login state. CAPTCHA/scan/pay handed back via ask tool + extension gate. No cloud vault.
entries.anti_bot: Relies on real user browser identity (fewer fresh-bot challenges). Not a stealth/CAPTCHA-solving cloud. Extension cannot inject into Chrome Web Store protected pages (documented negative case).
entries.pricing_summary: MIT; `npx huashu-chrome install`. Free. No paid plan found on product page.

entries.name: OpenCode Browse
entries.perception_note: README: agents drive tabs with Playwright, and execute exposes snapshot(). The same page also takes screenshots, captures network traffic, and records the screen. Documented mix of structured page access and screenshots (read 2026-11-02).
entries.hosting_note: Local MCP server plus a Chromium extension. npx @opencode/browse install puts the relay in ~/.local/share/opencode-browser. README: nothing leaves the computer except what the agent sends to its model provider.
entries.mcp_note: The product is an MCP server (browse) for OpenCode and other MCP clients. install writes it into OpenCode; other clients add the local stdio shim.
entries.auth_model_detail: Drives the Chromium profile you are signed in to. Logins, 2FA, and payments are handed back until you click Continue. Optional Deadbolt grants type stored secrets without putting the values in tool results (README Security, read 2026-11-02).
entries.anti_bot: README: Patchright hides navigator.webdriver and the Runtime.enable leak. Human-like input is on by default, and the page says this makes an agent hard to spot, not impossible. execute reports bot walls and never solves them; interactive challenges are handed to the user (read 2026-11-02).
entries.pricing_summary: MIT. npx @opencode/browse install. README: nothing to sign in to. No paid Browse plan found (read 2026-11-02).

entries.name: Foundry Browser Automation Tool
entries.perception_note: Unknown. The GA post and the how-to describe an observe-and-act loop and operator screenshot recording. They do not label the agent's own page reading as DOM, vision, or a mix (read 2026-11-02).
entries.hosting_note: Cloud. Playwright Workspaces provisions the isolated browser. The how-to says no local browser install is required. The workspace is a separate Azure resource.
entries.mcp_note: Foundry toolboxes expose an MCP-compatible endpoint for Browser Automation Tool. The how-to also points at the Playwright Workspaces remote MCP server for the tool list.
entries.auth_model_detail: Unknown for site logins. The how-to uses the Foundry project managed identity and a Playwright access token for Azure access, says to avoid pages that prompt for credentials, and describes Take control for a person to intervene. It does not describe a site-login vault (read 2026-11-02).
entries.anti_bot: Unknown. The GA post and the how-to do not describe stealth, CAPTCHA solving, or a fingerprint claim (read 2026-11-02).
entries.pricing_summary: Unknown. The GA post and the how-to do not state a Browser Automation Tool price. The how-to says sessions run in a Playwright workspace and points to that service's pricing docs without quoting a figure (read 2026-11-02).

entries.name: Auto Browser
entries.perception_note: README: Playwright sessions with screenshots, DOM summaries, and OCR excerpts (read 2026-11-02).
entries.hosting_note: Local-first Docker Compose. Published ports bind to 127.0.0.1 by default. GitHub Codespaces is documented as a quick demo, not a product cloud.
entries.mcp_note: HTTP MCP at http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp, plus a stdio bridge (uvx auto-browser-mcp or scripts/mcp_stdio_bridge.py).
entries.auth_model_detail: Named auth profiles: a person logs in during the session, including through noVNC takeover, and a later session can reopen that saved sign-in. README does not describe a placeholder vault (read 2026-11-02).
entries.anti_bot: README 'Not the Goal' lists CAPTCHA solving and deceptive identity or bypass tooling as out of scope (read 2026-11-02). The 1.10.0 notes mention a stealth-mode fix and do not describe a stealth product.
entries.pricing_summary: MIT. Local Docker Compose and GHCR images. No paid Auto Browser plan found on the README (read 2026-11-02).

entries.name: Browsentic
entries.perception_note: Page tools prefer selectors from page_getPageInfo. page_screenshot captures the page. Image captchas are read by a one-shot vision session (docs/guide/features/captcha.md, read 2026-11-02).
entries.hosting_note: Local-first. The extension dials Browsentic Bridge on 127.0.0.1. README: no cloud component. macOS and Windows apps install the Bridge; npx browsentic@latest setup is the Node path.
entries.mcp_note: The side panel and an agent CLI you already run are the primary path. An optional MCP server drives the same browser (https://browsentic.com/mcp-server/, read 2026-11-02).
entries.auth_model_detail: Acts in the browser you are already signed in to. README: credentials on a page are sealed before the agent sees them. No Browsentic account (read 2026-11-02).
entries.anti_bot: Captcha doc: a real click ticks the checkbox, and a short-lived vision session answers image challenges. Arkose, AWS WAF, and drag-to-fit are handed back. Solving is approval-gated. No pass rate on that page (read 2026-11-02).
entries.pricing_summary: Apache-2.0. README: versions through 0.7.15 were MIT. No account, no API key, and no extra Browsentic subscription. No $/mo found (read 2026-11-02).

entries.name: better-browser-mcp
entries.perception_note: README: compact text snapshots (role, name, ref) and batched act calls, positioned against screenshot loops. Not a vision-first agent (read 2026-11-02).
entries.hosting_note: Local MCP server plus an unpacked Chrome extension. README: stdio and a paired local WebSocket, no cloud relay. The GitHub URL redirects to alexsorokoletov/bopbop (checked 2026-11-02). The README title and the 2026-10-29 post still say better-browser-mcp.
entries.mcp_note: MCP server for any MCP client. The README quick start runs prototype/src/server.ts with bun or node and loads the extension unpacked.
entries.auth_model_detail: Extension mode drives your real Chrome profile and its sign-ins. Agent tabs sit in their own tab group. No cloud credential vault is described (read 2026-11-02).
entries.anti_bot: Unknown. The README and the 2026-10-29 post do not claim stealth, CAPTCHA solving, or a fingerprint product (read 2026-11-02).
entries.pricing_summary: MIT. LICENSE copyright (c) 2026 Alex Sorokoletov. Local open-source install. No paid plan found on the README or the announcement (read 2026-11-02).

entries.name: Browserbase (infra companion — not a separate agent row)
entries.perception_note: Cloud browser host used by Stagehand. Not a matrix row.
entries.mcp_note: Hosted MCP documented for Browserbase (Stagehand-oriented tools).
entries.anti_bot: Stealth/proxy/session features for cloud browsers (vendor marketing).
entries.pricing_summary: Host rates, read 2026-10-24 at browserbase.com/pricing and docs.browserbase.com/account/billing/plans: Free $0, Developer $20/mo, Startup $99/mo, Scale custom. Browser-hour overage: Developer $0.12/hr, Startup $0.10/hr. Not a Stagehand price.
entries.note: Browserbase hosts browsers for Stagehand and other agents. It is not listed here as an agent.

changelog_seed.item: Added OpenCode Browse, Foundry Browser Automation Tool, Auto Browser, Browsentic, and better-browser-mcp from public docs. OpenCode Browse: GitHub repo created 2026-10-27; MindPattern note published 2026-10-29; no official demo video. Foundry Browser Automation Tool: GA post 2026-10-19; the post and the how-to do not state a price; the Microsoft Developer clip plays in the row (YouTube title: Browser Automation Tool (Preview)). Auto Browser: v1.11.0 published 2026-10-24 and v1.12.1 published 2026-10-30; the README demo is a GIF, so this row has no video. Browsentic: v0.9.0 published 2026-10-18, repository push 2026-10-27; a homepage mp4 plays in the row. better-browser-mcp: announcement 2026-10-29; a repository mp4 plays in the row. No star counts were added.

Added ego (lite), xbrowser, agent-browser, and huashu-chrome from public docs. Official demo video plays in the row panel where a vendor clip exists. Skyvern, xbrowser, agent-browser, and huashu-chrome have no official clip; huashu-chrome shows the repository architecture diagram. The interface is available in Chinese and English.

Notte perception set to hybrid from observe (action space plus screenshot) and agent-start use_vision default true. OpenAI credentials set to app-owned / driver-dependent. Sample-app LICENSE read as MIT, Copyright (c) 2025 OpenAI. Smooth added. Stagehand still has no $/hour; the Browserbase host page is linked from that row.
Anthropic announced Claude in Chrome generally available on all paid Claude plans, with autonomous browser actions gated by a safety classifier.
Browser Use public materials and docs center on Cloud Agents API v4 (runs/sessions/browsers) and related Harness/changelog updates (e.g. Browser Harness API notes around mid-July 2026).
Stagehand v4 docs/migration guides are live (act/extract/observe + browser factories; v3→v4 migration pages).
Playwright MCP releases added WebMCP tools-as-MCP-tools and related agent UX (e.g. v0.0.82 highlights around 18 Sep 2026 per GitHub releases).

excluded_or_deferred.name: LaVague
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Third-party comparisons note active development ended ~Jan 2025; not seeded as an active row without confirming current maintenance.

excluded_or_deferred.name: AgentQL
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Semantic query/extraction layer over Playwright, not a full autonomous browser-agent framework — out of primary matrix scope.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Pure cloud browser hosts (Steel, Browserless, Hyperbrowser, etc.)
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Infra $/hour layer — deliberately out of Browserly scope.
